column1: # The stages of the integration, in order, one row per stage — which is one row
# per commit. Tab-separated: slug <TAB> name <TAB> what it gives you.
# The slug names the stage's frozen figures (measurements/<slug>.csv) and is what
# scripts/run.sh builds; the last row is the stage under construction. A stage's
# row is added when its work starts and its CSV frozen when the figures settle,
# so the two are briefly out of step — the cost table leaves an unfrozen stage
# out and says so rather than publishing a blank row.
# Slugs, not numbers: a stage inserted mid-history would renumber every file

column3: a device that already networks, stores, and holds an mTLS session — before any syslog
the core library and lwIP raw-mode networking, linked but not yet called
a fault inside the logger reaches the console instead of being silent
the logger object, reporting exactly what is still missing from it
a valid RFC 5424 record on the wire, over UDP
a timestamped record naming the device, instead of nil values
every record numbered, so a gap in the sequence is visible
logging that returns immediately, with the send moved off the logging task
records the network retransmits instead of dropping, and a send that fails when the collector is gone
a timestamp the collector knows how far to trust, and an uptime that tells a reboot from a counter wrap
records that survive a failed send, spooled to disk with a checksum at rest
the device named in the record itself, not inferred from the source address
the device's own address in the record, which a relay or NAT between it and the collector cannot rewrite
a collector the device authenticates, and records no longer readable on the wire
stored records that cannot be edited undetected, not merely checked for corruption
a record that states the protection its own log pipeline was under
